Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

REWORK round 1 on Step 6 (ZimmProductCard organism). Three bounded fixes, all independently verified by Tester/Orchestrator via real computed-style rendering and direct Figma metadata — not guesses.

## Files to modify (only these 2, unless a test needs a specific new/updated assertion)
```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx
```
Do not touch `index.tsx` or `index.stories.tsx` for fixes 1-2 (pure CSS fixes). Fix 3 may need one line in `index.tsx` — see below. Do NOT touch `zimmProductCardMedia/`, `zimmProductCardContent/`, or any other already-committed file.

## Fix 1 — the close-button lift rule breaks its own positioning (real, currently-visible bug)

Current code in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`:
```ts
'[data-card-slot="close"]': { position: 'relative', zIndex: 1 },
```

This is wrong and was proven wrong by rendering the REAL composed tree (no mocks) and reading `getComputedStyle`: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` recipe part (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`) already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact element — that's how the remove button gets pinned to the top-right corner of the image. The organism's lift rule uses a class+attribute-selector descendant combinator (`.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]`), which has HIGHER CSS specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so the organism's `position: 'relative'` WINS the cascade and silently overrides Media's `position: 'absolute'` — the button falls out of its pinned position into normal document flow, below the image, for every Wishlist card, on first paint, no hover or interaction needed.

**Fix:** remove `position: 'relative'` from this one lift rule — leave only `zIndex: 1`:
```ts
'[data-card-slot="close"]': { zIndex: 1 },
```
The element is ALREADY positioned (`position: absolute`, set by Media's own recipe) — for `z-index` to take effect, an element only needs to BE positioned (any value other than `static`), it doesn't matter which component's recipe made it positioned. Adding a competing `position` value here was never necessary and is what broke it.

**Do NOT touch the other two lift rules** (`[data-card-slot="carousel"] button`, `[data-card-slot="content"] button`) — those target elements that have NO prior `position` set in their own component recipes (confirmed: Media's arrow buttons and Content's bag/notify-me buttons are all `position: static` by default in their own recipes), so `position: 'relative'` is a safe, necessary, non-destructive addition for THOSE two rules specifically. This fix is scoped to the ONE rule that targets an element that was already positioned by its owning component.

**Verify the fix, don't just apply it:** render the real composed organism (real theme, no `useMultiStyleConfig` mock — same technique already used elsewhere in this test file for the "real recipe assertions" block) for `variation="wishlist"`, and assert via `getComputedStyle` on the close button that `position` is `"absolute"` (not `"relative"`) and `top`/`right` are both `"0px"`, proving the button is genuinely pinned to the image's top-right corner again. Add this as a new test case if the file doesn't already have one checking the close button's actual computed position (it currently only checks `zIndex`/generic lift behaviour, per the Tester's report — read the existing tests first to confirm exactly what's missing before adding).

## Fix 2 — size chips are unreachable by keyboard (confirmed UNDER-scope: an explicit Step 6 pass criterion, not met)

Current code hides the size-chip slot via `display: 'none'` unconditionally, revealing it ONLY inside `&:hover` nested under the hover-capable media query:
```ts
// current shape, read the real file for exact line numbers before editing
[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
  '&:hover [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'block' },
  // (similar for price hiding)
},
```
`display: none` removes an element from the tab order entirely — a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable desktop (a mouse-and-keyboard user who's currently tabbing, not hovering) can NEVER focus into the size chips on a PLP/Wishlist card, because nothing except an actual pointer hover ever reveals them.

**Fix:** add `:focus-within` alongside `:hover` on every reveal rule that currently only checks `&:hover`, mirroring the exact syntax already established in this codebase — read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSearchInput/zimmSearchInput.css.ts` (around line 30) and `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (around lines 261, 278) for the precedent pattern (likely `&:hover, &:focus-within` as a single compound selector, or Chakra's `_focusWithin` key alongside `_hover` — check which idiom those two files actually use and match it exactly, don't invent a third variant). Apply this to BOTH the size-chip reveal rule AND the price-hide rule (if hovering hides price, focus-within on the card should also hide price, for the same reason — keyboard and mouse users should see the identical revealed state, not two different partial states).

**The `:focus-within` needs to be scoped to the right ancestor.** Check exactly what element the `&:hover`/`&:focus-within` compound needs to attach to — it should trigger when focus is ANYWHERE within the composed card (e.g. when the size chips themselves, or the name link, or the bag button receives focus via Tab), which means `:focus-within` needs to be on the ORGANISM's own root (the same element `&:hover` is presumably already scoped to) so that focusing ANY descendant control reveals the size chips — not scoped narrowly to just the size-chip wrapper itself (which would be circular: you can't focus-within an element that's display:none and therefore unfocusable and unreachable by Tab in the first place).

**Verify:** add a test that simulates focus landing on a descendant of the card root (e.g. `fireEvent.focus()` on the bag button, or use `userEvent.tab()` to a focusable descendant) and asserts, via the real unmocked recipe object AND/OR a real rendered DOM check, that the size-chip slot's computed `display` is no longer `none` once something inside the card has focus. Use the same "import the real recipe module directly" technique already established in this file for the hover-reveal structural tests, PLUS a real-DOM interaction test if that's more natural for proving the `:focus-within` CSS actually engages during a real focus event (CSS `:focus-within` DOES work correctly in jsdom — unlike layout/hit-testing, pseudo-class matching during real DOM focus events is something jsdom implements correctly, so this one IS meaningfully testable, unlike the z-index stacking concern from Fix 1's category).

## Fix 3 — mobile PLP/PDP cards show the bag icon, but Figma hides it there

Confirmed via direct Figma inspection (node `40002163:41477`/`40002163:41479`, Mobile/Default/PLP-PDP): the bag icon (`Icons` frame) is `hidden="true"` on mobile. On Desktop, the same PLP/PDP card always shows it. The current `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBag` in `index.tsx` is a single boolean per variation (true for PLP/Wishlist) with no mobile/desktop distinction, so mobile PLP cards currently render the bag icon when they shouldn't.

**This needs a CSS-level fix, not a VARIATION_CONFIG/JSX change** — keep `showBag` exactly as-is (Content still renders the bag button in the DOM for PLP regardless of viewport; this preserves Content's own simple boolean contract and avoids adding viewport-awareness to a component that has no other breakpoint logic). Instead, add a responsive rule to `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s `root` part that hides the bag wrapper below the desktop breakpoint:

Read how `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` part expresses its desktop breakpoint (added in a prior Step 5 fix — it imports `breakpoints` from `app/theme/foundation` and uses `` [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`] `` as the desktop-and-up key). Match that exact import path and breakpoint token in `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (import `breakpoints` the same way if not already imported here).

Add a rule targeting the bag button's own rendered location. Check `ZimmProductCardContent`'s actual DOM structure first (read `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`) to find the correct selector for the bag button specifically — it does NOT carry a `data-card-slot` attribute of its own (only `content`/`price`/`sizeChips` do, per Content's own documented contract), so you likely need to target it by its accessible role/attribute shape (e.g. a `button` inside `[data-card-slot="content"]` that is NOT inside `[data-card-slot="sizeChips"]` — check whether a simple `[data-card-slot="content"] > * button` or similar over-broad selector would accidentally also hide the notify-me button, which is a DIFFERENT control that should NOT be hidden on mobile). If no clean CSS selector can distinguish "the bag button specifically" from Content's OTHER buttons without over-reaching, STOP and report this precisely as a real architectural gap requiring either a new `data-card-slot` value on Content's bag button (which would mean touching the already-committed `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` — flag this as needing sign-off before doing it, don't silently expand scope into a previously-committed file) rather than inventing a fragile selector. Do not ship a selector that might accidentally hide the wrong control.

**This gate is PLP-specific, not Home/Wishlist** — Home never shows the bag at all (any viewport); confirm from Figma citations already established in this build whether Wishlist's mobile variant ALSO hides the bag (check if a Wishlist mobile node was ever resolved in this build's history — if not, do not assume Wishlist behaves the same as PLP; scope this fix to PLP only unless you find confirming evidence for Wishlist too, and say explicitly in your report whether you found or could not find that evidence).

## After all three fixes, verify:
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
All must be clean/green. Confirm via `git status --porcelain` that only `zimmProductCard/` files (plus the unchanged pre-existing diffs from earlier steps, if any remain — there should be none left uncommitted from Step 5) show any change. Do NOT stage or commit — this step still needs a real-browser visual/interaction check after these fixes land.

Report exactly what changed for each fix, and if Fix 3 hit the "no clean selector" wall described above, stop there and report precisely rather than guessing.
